title: Learning: Contiguity Theory, Instrumental Conditioning, Operant Conditioning
summary: Contiguity theory of learning; instrumental conditioning; law of readiness; operant conditioning; reinforcement (positive/negative); punishment; continuous reinforcement; Premack principle; learned helplessness.
objectives: Explain Thorndike's law of readiness and law of effect.
Describe operant conditioning and reinforcement types.
Explain Premack principle and learned helplessness.
revision: Operant conditioning: behavior shaped by consequences. Reinforcement increases behavior; punishment decreases. Premack = preferred reinforces less preferred. Learned helplessness = passivity from uncontrollable aversive events.
traps: Premack principle = preferred activity reinforces less preferred.

notes.t: Contiguity theory proposes that learning occurs when stimuli and responses occur together in time and space, without requiring reinforcement.
Instrumental conditioning (Thorndike) proposes that responses followed by satisfying consequences are strengthened (law of effect).
Thorndike's law of readiness: when a conduction unit is ready to conduct, doing so is satisfying; when forced not to conduct, it is annoying.
Operant conditioning: behavior is shaped by its consequences. Reinforcement increases behavior; punishment decreases behavior.
Continuous reinforcement: every correct response is reinforced. Fast acquisition but rapid extinction.
A more preferred activity can reinforce a less preferred activity.
Learned helplessness: exposure to uncontrollable aversive events leads to passivity and failure to escape even when escape is possible.
UGC NET frequently asks about operant conditioning reinforcement types and the Premack principle.

mnemonics.title: PRNP
mnemonics.text: Positive reinforcement → add reward (increase behavior), Negative reinforcement → remove aversive (increase behavior), Positive punishment → add aversive (decrease behavior), Negative punishment → remove reward (decrease behavior)

flashcards.a: More preferred activity reinforces less preferred activity.
